cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still giving his big speech to the people. Now he puts one little word on the table that carries a LOT of weight: if they faithfully obey the voice of the LORD their God and carefully follow all His commandments. Friend, when Moses says 'if,' I lean in.

cards.question: If Israel obeys, where does Moses say the LORD their God will set them?

answers.text: Back in the land of Egypt

cards.text: Moses says these blessings will come upon them and OVERTAKE them. Blessings that chase you DOWN, friend, when usually the only thing that catches up with you like that is a late fee.

cards.question: Moses starts listing the blessings, and the list covers a lot of ground. Where does he say Israel will be blessed?

answers.text: In the city and in the country
In the temple and in the palace
In the desert and by the sea

cards.question: True or false: Moses says the blessings will reach their children, their crops and even the calves and lambs of their herds and flocks.

cards.text: Then Moses blesses something I know VERY well. Friend, this one comes straight out of the kitchen.

cards.question: Along with their basket, what kitchen item does Moses say will be blessed?

cards.text: A BLESSED kneading bowl. I'm not crying, friend, there's just a little flour in my eye.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says Israel will be blessed when they come in, but warns them to watch out when they go out.
Then Moses turns to enemies who rise up against Israel. The LORD will defeat them, and they'll march out in one direction but flee in ___.

cards.text: One direction in, SEVEN directions out. I've seen that exact move in an office break room when somebody spots a spider.
Moses keeps the list rolling. The LORD will decree a blessing on their barns and on everything they put their hand to, right there in the land He's giving them.

cards.question: Then Moses goes bigger than barns. If they keep the LORD's commandments, He'll establish them as His ___ people, just as He swore to them.

cards.text: And there's that 'if' again: if they keep His commandments and walk in His ways. Moses keeps saying it, like a recipe that won't stop reminding you to preheat the oven.

cards.question: When all the peoples of the earth see that Israel is called by the name of the LORD, how will they react?

answers.text: They'll stand in awe of them

cards.text: Moses circles back to their children, their livestock and their crops. This time he says the LORD will make them prosper abundantly in the land He swore to their fathers.

cards.question: Moses calls the heavens the LORD's abundant storehouse. He'll open them to send ___ on their land in season.
True or false: Moses says Israel will borrow from many nations.

cards.text: Nope. They'll LEND to many nations and borrow from NONE, and friend, I'm just sitting here imagining never opening a 'payment due' email again.

cards.question: Next Moses paints a picture of Israel's place among the nations. What will the LORD make them?

answers.text: The head and not the tail
The hands and not the feet
The eyes and not the ears

cards.text: They'll only move upward and never downward, if they hear and carefully follow the LORD's commandments. Friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, I'd have thrown a PARTY for sideways.

cards.question: Moses wraps up with a warning about all the words he's commanding them today. What does he tell them not to do?

answers.text: Turn aside to the right or the left
Add new words of their own

cards.question: True or false: Moses also warns Israel not to go after other gods to serve them.

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause for now. But keep your apron on, friend, because Moses isn't done preaching.

findings.problem: 'Then Moses blesses something' says Moses is doing the blessing. The text says only that the basket and kneading bowl 'will be blessed' (Deut 28:5). It does not say Moses blesses them.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the kneading bowl answer from card 7 and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of the line ('flee in ___'). The number seven can't be reasoned out from earlier cards, so this tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the 'seven directions' answer from card 10 and adds a joke. It adds nothing from the passage. It is a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Add new words of their own' is close in meaning to not turning aside from the words Moses commands. Moses also forbids adding to his words elsewhere (Deut 4:2; 12:32), so a baker could argue this answer is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
